title: Monocots vs Dicots Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Hold a blade of grass and a mango leaf up to the light: one has straight lines, the other has a net. Diya wants to know why, and that one clue splits every flowering plant into two big groups.

You will see what angiosperm means, zoom from a flower into its ovary, an ovule and the seven-celled embryo sac, and watch double fertilisation run step by step: the pollen tube, syngamy and triple fusion. Then monocots and dicots side by side (cotyledons, roots, leaf veins, stem bundles, flower parts), a pause and think check, a worked sort of six plants, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question, a recap card and three questions to answer. This is Episode 26 of our PUC Biology series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.

In this video:

3:59 Exam trap: is a dicot a plant with two seeds?
